content: Cefprozil demonstrates in vitro activity against a wide spectrum of both gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria. Its bactericidal effect is achieved through the inhibition of bacterial cell wall synthesis. Cefprozil has been shown to be effective against most strains of specific microorganisms in both in vitro studies and clinical infections, as outlined in the Indications and Usage section. Aerobic Gram-Positive Microorganisms: Staphylococcus aureus (including β-lactamase-producing strains). Note: Cefprozil is not effective against methicillin-resistant staphylococci (MRSA). Streptococcus pneumoniae. Streptococcus pyogenes. Aerobic Gram-Negative Microorganisms: Haemophilus influenzae (including β-lactamase-producing strains). Moraxella (Branhamella) catarrhalis (including β-lactamase-producing strains). Additional In Vitro Data: Cefprozil exhibits minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of ≤8 mcg/mL against most (≥90%) strains of the following microorganisms. However, the clinical significance of these findings is uncertain, as the safety and efficacy of cefprozil in treating infections caused by these organisms have not been established in well-controlled clinical trials. Aerobic Gram-Positive Microorganisms: Enterococcus durans. Enterococcus faecalis. Listeria monocytogenes. Staphylococcus epidermidis. Staphylococcus saprophyticus. Staphylococcus warneri. Streptococcus agalactiae. Streptococci (Groups C, D, F, and G). Viridans group streptococci. Note: Cefprozil is not effective against Enterococcus faecium. Aerobic Gram-Negative Microorganisms: Citrobacter diversus. Escherichia coli. Klebsiella pneumoniae. Neisseria gonorrhoeae (including β-lactamase-producing strains). Proteus mirabilis. Salmonella spp.. Shigella spp.. Vibrio spp.. Note: Cefprozil is not effective against most strains of Acinetobacter, Enterobacter, Morganella morganii, Proteus vulgaris, Providencia, Pseudomonas, and Serratia. Anaerobic Microorganisms: Prevotella (Bacteroides) melaninogenicus. Clostridium difficile. Clostridium perfringens. Fusobacterium spp.. Peptostreptococcus spp.. Propionibacterium acnes. Note: Most strains of the Bacteroides fragilis group are resistant to cefprozil. Susceptibility Testing: Dilution Techniques: Quantitative methods are used to determine the minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of antimicrobial agents, which estimate the susceptibility of bacteria to these compounds. MICs should be determined using standardized procedures, such as broth or agar dilution methods, with standardized inoculum concentrations and cefprozil powder concentrations. The MIC values should be interpreted as follows: Susceptible: Indicates that the pathogen is likely to be inhibited if the antimicrobial compound in the blood reaches concentrations typically achievable. Intermediate: Suggests equivocal results. If the microorganism is not fully susceptible to alternative, clinically feasible drugs, the test should be repeated. This category may have clinical applicability in body sites where the drug is physiologically concentrated or when high dosages can be used. It also provides a buffer zone to account for minor technical variations. Resistant: Indicates that the pathogen is unlikely to be inhibited at achievable blood concentrations of the antimicrobial compound, and alternative therapy should be selected. Standardized susceptibility testing requires the use of laboratory control microorganisms to ensure the technical accuracy of the procedures. Standard cefprozil powder should yield specific MIC values for quality control. Diffusion Techniques: Quantitative methods involving the measurement of zone diameters also provide reproducible estimates of bacterial susceptibility to antimicrobial agents. A standardized procedure involves the use of paper disks impregnated with 30 mcg of cefprozil to test microorganism susceptibility. Results from the single-disk susceptibility test should be interpreted in correlation with MIC values for cefprozil. As with dilution techniques, diffusion methods require laboratory control microorganisms to ensure procedural accuracy. For the diffusion technique, the 30 mcg cefprozil disk should produce specific zone diameters in quality control strains.
